metadata.note: The Ware River Railroad: Palmer - Thorndike - Ware - Gilbertville - Barre Plains - South Barre - Barre - Coldbrook - Williamsville - Templeton - Baldwinville - Waterville - Winchendon, MA, 49.4 mi (Fowler). The Ware River company appears never to have run its own trains except possibly in its 1870 opening year: Palmer - Gilbertville (opened 1870) was worked by the New London Northern until 1873, then the line passed to the Boston and Albany (purchase April 1873 per Karr; 999-year lease from 1 Jan 1874 per the corporate abstract), which completed it to Winchendon in November 1873 and ran it as its Ware River Branch. Features are split by operator (Rule 4) and at Gilbertville, where the opening year changes. The B&A name and colour are kept after the 1900 NYC&HR lease, as in boston_and_albany_railroad.geojson. Both B&A features end at 1918, the last CONFIRMED public-timetable year, not a known end.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (schedules eff. 30 Sept 1951), index: Coldbrook, Gilbertville, South Barre, Templeton, Ware marked New York Central 'For freight only'
Ronald D. Karr, The Rail Lines of Southern New England (Branch Line Press, 1995), pp.184-185 - cited page by page by WP-PU; not consulted directly
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), traced 2026-10-16 with opstrace.py on the rail degree-tiles plus every way tagged old_railway_operator ~ NYC / New York Central / Boston & Albany in the corridor (ex-B&A track in Massachusetts is tagged old_railway_operator=NYC) and every way NAMED 'Ware River ...' (the Ware River Rail Trail between Barre and Baldwinville carries no operator tag), counted as own track; rail-trail and abandoned ways were fetched separately over South Barre - Waterville and Waterville - Winchendon. OpenHistoricalMap was queried for both lifted stretches and returned no ways. Waypoints are OSM place nodes for each station village (Thorndike, Ware, Gilbertville, Barre Plains, South Barre, Coldbrook Springs, Williamsville, Templeton Station, Baldwinville, Waterville) and hand-pinned points at Palmer (Union Station) and Winchendon (the B&A/Cheshire junction at the B&M depot, where cheshire_railroad.geojson ends); Nominatim was not used. Each waypoint lies 0.0-0.5 km from the drawn line.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Built to Rule 1 from the start: nothing is drawn after 1918, the last confirmed passenger year. Not drawn: freight after passenger service ended (Penn Central 1968, Conrail Palmer - Ware to 1979, Massachusetts Central Railroad Palmer - South Barre since 1979; South Barre - Waterville to 1968; B&M Waterville - Winchendon to 1984); the 1933-41 B&M Central Mass trackage-rights freights over the branch (Barre Jct - Creamery - Forest Lake Jct); and any year attested only by the 1924/1949/1957 employee timetables.
metadata.horsecar_audit: Nothing to remove: a steam railroad from its 1870 opening.
metadata.colour_note: No new colours. New London Northern Railroad and Boston and Albany Railroad colours pulled programmatically from new_london_northern_railroad.geojson and boston_and_albany_railroad.geojson; every feature with each company string across data/ was confirmed to share one colour.
not_yet_sourced: END DATE of passenger service, both B&A features [OPEN at 1918]: 1918 is the last public timetable seen. Karr p.185 (via WP-PU): 'A mixed train was operated on the Ware River Branch until 1948' - extent (whole line? Palmer - Ware?) and when regular passenger trains gave way to it are not established; checking Karr pp.184-185 directly, or a 'last train' item in the Barre Gazette / Ware River News / Gardner News, could move either end to 1948 or earlier. The Feb 1952 Official Guide daggers the stations freight only, so service ended before Sept 1951.

No source in hand confirms passenger service in 1921 or 1932: Fowler's B&A/NYC timetable letters (1903, 1921, 1932, 1952) are absent from every Ware River station even though the 1916 and 1918 public timetables print the branch. Treated as absence of evidence, not as an end.

1873/1874 changeover: April 1873 purchase by the B&A (Karr via WP-PU) vs. foreclosure 22 May 1873, reorganization 12 Jun 1873 and B&A lease from 1 Jan 1874 (Scripophily abstract) vs. Chester Chapin's personal purchase (Railpace); and who ran the Nov-Dec 1873 trains to Winchendon (Gilbertville - Winchendon drawn from 1874 for that reason).
1870 operator (Palmer - Gilbertville opening year withheld): possibly the Ware River company itself; NLN lease 'shortly after opening' (Railpace).

NLN vs. Vermont Central for 1871-1873: Karr says the Vermont Central (which he dates as leasing the NLN in 1871) ran the trains until April 1873; new_london_northern_railroad.geojson dates the NLN's lease to the Central Vermont 25 Jun 1873. Not split on the disputed date.
Through running: whether Ware River trains ran through Palmer to Springfield or over the NLN - no timetable body seen.
Every headway_min (480, i.e. a few trains a day) and avg_speed_kmh (30) is an estimate; no train count or running time was seen for any year.
Coldbrook-area alignment (Ware River watershed / Barre Falls Dam): whether the OSM grade is the original 1873 alignment.

segments.note: The Ware River Railroad (incorporated 16 Mar 1867) opened Palmer - Thorndike - Ware - Gilbertville in 1870 and was worked by the New London Northern, with which it shared a right of way north of Palmer: 'operated by the New London Northern ... in 1871 and the Vermont Central Railroad until April 1873 when it was bought by the B&A' (Karr pp.184-185 via Wikipedia); 'until 1873 it was leased to and operated by the New London Northern' (WP-MCER); 'shortly after opening, the road was leased to the NLN' (Railpace). 1870 is withheld because who ran the opening-year trains is not established (possibly the Ware River company itself). Karr's wording implies the NLN's own lessee, the Vermont Central, ran the trains 1871-73, whereas new_london_northern_railroad.geojson has the NLN running its own trains until the Central Vermont lease of 25 Jun 1873; both readings are recorded and the feature is not split on that disputed date. The 1873 end is the operator boundary (B&A purchase April 1873 per Karr), not a gap. No timetable or train count found; headway is an estimate.

segments.note: Boston and Albany 'Ware River Branch'. Start: the B&A bought the line in April 1873 (Karr via WP-PU) - but the corporate abstract (Scripophily) has the road sold under foreclosure 22 May 1873, reorganized 12 Jun 1873 and LEASED to the B&A from 1 Jan 1874 for 999 years, and Railpace says B&A president Chester Chapin bought it personally and later sold it to the B&A; drawn from 1873, the operator-boundary year, with the conflict in not_yet_sourced. Printed in B&A public timetables of 17 Jun 1894, 1 Aug 1916 and 20 Oct 1918 (Nashua City Station); 1924/1949/1957 employee timetables also list the stations but prove nothing about passengers. The B&A name is kept after the 1900 NYC&HR lease, per the convention of boston_and_albany_railroad.geojson. Passenger service confirmed to 1918 by the USRA 'Boston and Albany Railroad Time Tables - Corrected to October 20, 1918' public timetable (station list via Nashua City Station). This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. Karr (p.185, via Wikipedia) says a mixed train ran on the Ware River Branch until 1948, extent not stated; the Feb 1952 Official Guide index marks these stations freight only. Do not extend without evidence. Freight continued (Penn Central 1968, Conrail to 1979, Massachusetts Central since). Headway is an estimate: no train count was seen for any year.
sources: Segment-level: start from Karr pp.184-185 via WP-PU, Scripophily abstract and Railpace; 1918 last-confirmed year from the 20 Oct 1918 USRA B&A public timetable station list on Nashua City Station (also 1894, 1916). End is NOT SOURCED as an actual end. (research/branches/ware_river_railroad.txt compiled these from the cited pages; the tracer did not re-read the source text)

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 33.2 mi against documented 33.6 mi Gilbertville - Winchendon (Fowler line 50: 49.4 - 15.8), 1.2% short. No straight-line legs. Gilbertville - South Barre on the live 'Ware River Secondary' (OSM NYC); South Barre - Coldbrook on NYC-tagged abandoned ways, except ~0.4 mi east of South Barre (lon -72.065 to -72.058) drawn on OSM way 296592839, NAMED 'Mass Central Rail Trail', which joins the NYC-tagged B&A grade ways at both ends while the B&M Central Mass grade is mapped separately ~100 m south (ways 1309501271/1152316837) - so it is taken to be the B&A grade under a trail name, not the B&M line (not field-verified); Coldbrook - Williamsville - Templeton - Baldwinville on the Ware River Rail Trail; Baldwinville - Waterville - Winchendon on the abandoned 'Ware River Rail Trail' and NYC-tagged ways into the B&M depot; 0.1 mi of short connector joins between adjacent mapped ways. Traced mileposts from Gilbertville against Fowler: Barre Plains 7.8 (8.0), South Barre 8.8 (9.0), Coldbrook 11.1 (11.3), Williamsville 17.0 (17.4), Templeton 23.2 (23.3), Baldwinville 26.7 (27.0), Waterville 31.6 (31.8), Winchendon 33.2 (33.6). ERA CAVEATS: the line was lifted South Barre - Waterville in 1968 and Waterville - Winchendon after 1984, so the grade is drawn as OSM maps it after abandonment; whether the grade through the Coldbrook / Barre Falls Dam (USACE, 1958) flood-control area is the original 1873 alignment or a later relocation is not established; at the Route 2 embankment north of Templeton the drawn line follows the mapped grade, not the modern on-road trail detour.

segments.note: Gilbertville - Barre Plains - South Barre - Barre - Coldbrook - Williamsville (Hubbardston) - Templeton - Baldwinville - Waterville - Winchendon, joining the Cheshire (Fitchburg, later B&M) at Winchendon. Completed November 1873 ('completed to Winchendon that November', Karr via WP-PU; 'opened in November, 1873', Scripophily abstract). 1873 is withheld because who ran the Nov-Dec 1873 trains is ambiguous (B&A purchase April 1873 per Karr; Chapin personal ownership per Railpace; B&A lease only from 1 Jan 1874 per the abstract); 1874 is the first year the B&A is the documented lessee. Stations to Winchendon printed in the Pathfinder Guide 1876 and 1894 (Fowler) and in B&A public timetables of 1894, 1916 and 1918 (Nashua City Station). Passenger service confirmed to 1918 by the USRA 'Boston and Albany Railroad Time Tables - Corrected to October 20, 1918' public timetable (station list via Nashua City Station). This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. Karr (p.185, via Wikipedia) says a mixed train ran on the Ware River Branch until 1948, extent not stated; the Feb 1952 Official Guide index marks these stations freight only. Do not extend without evidence. Whether Karr's 1948 mixed train ran north of Ware/Gilbertville is not known. Lifted South Barre - Waterville 1968; the B&M worked Waterville - Winchendon for freight until 1984. Headway is an estimate: no train count was seen for any year.
sources: Segment-level: November 1873 completion from Karr pp.184-185 via WP-PU and the Scripophily abstract; 1874 B&A lease from the abstract; 1918 last-confirmed year from the 20 Oct 1918 USRA B&A public timetable station list on Nashua City Station (also 1894, 1916). End is NOT SOURCED as an actual end. (research/branches/ware_river_railroad.txt compiled these from the cited pages; the tracer did not re-read the source text)
